note: Written by the case seat (WriteOomKillersCases) before any tool exists. Compare expect.verdict, expect.exit and only the dotted paths present in expect.fields. Every MESSAGE string is derived from the earlyoom v1.9.0 format strings (main.c, kill.c, msg.h at tag v1.9.0); every process name in this file is invented. The `error` field required by contract.md:105 is intentionally not pinned: its text is implementation defined, so only verdict and exit are asserted for the error cases.

cases.why: Host shaped quiet case. earlyoom 1.9.0 prints its version at main.c:161 (`fprintf(stderr, "earlyoom " VERSION "\n")`), then the term thresholds at main.c:414 (`sending SIGTERM when mem avail <= PRIPCT and swap free <= PRIPCT,`) and the kill thresholds at main.c:416 (`SIGKILL when mem avail <= PRIPCT and swap free <= PRIPCT`, indented by eight spaces). PRIPCT is `"%5.2lf%%"` (msg.h:10), so a one digit percent renders with a pad space: ` 5.00%`. The thresholds must therefore parse to the numbers 10.0/10.0/5.0/5.0, not to strings. The `mem total:` and `mem avail:` lines (main.c:412, meminfo.c:279) and the systemd `Started Early OOM Daemon.` line are outside the grammar (contract.md:80) and must be ignored; their memory figures are invented, only the thresholds 10.00/10.00/5.00/5.00 are the host configuration. Version line at 19981126 is inside the scope (>= ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic 19964362), so scope_complete is true (contract.md:90) and the grammar is verified-1.9.0. No action, escalation, kill_failed or low memory line is in scope and oomd notices are 0, so no positive evidence exists and the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0 (contract.md:97-104).

sending SIGTERM when mem avail <= 10.00% and swap free <= 10.00%,
SIGKILL when mem avail <=  5.00% and swap free <=  5.00%
mem avail: 12000 of 19000 MiB (63.16%), swap free: 8000 of 8192 MiB (97.66%)

cases.why: Scope boundary, lower side. contract.md:78 scopes earlyoom lines to `__MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP` >= `ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic` of the current invocation, so a line stamped one microsecond before 19964362 is out of scope. The action line uses the kill.c:627 form `sending %s to process %d uid %d "%s": ...`; only the invented process name is kept and the uid and cmdline parts are dropped, because the case file must not carry uid or command line values. The action is out of scope, so it is not positive evidence (contract.md:97) and the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0 with the action counts at zero. The version line at exactly 19964362 is inside the scope, so scope_complete stays true.

Scope boundary, upper side. Same inputs as c02 with the action line stamped exactly at 19964362, which contract.md:78 puts inside the scope (>=, not >). The line is the kill.c:627 form `sending %s to process %d ...` with the invented name `imaginary-keeper`. An in scope `sending SIGTERM to process` line is positive evidence (contract.md:97), so the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1 and the sigterm count is 1 while the sigkill count stays 0.

Incomplete scope that still holds an action. The version line (main.c:161) is stamped one microsecond before ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic, so it is out of scope and scope_complete is false (contract.md:90: true only when the version line of the current invocation is inside the scope). The action line at 19970000 is inside the scope, and contract.md:97 says positive evidence stands even when the scope is incomplete, so the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1 and not KILLERS_UNKNOWN. Without a version line in scope the grammar cannot be confirmed as 1.9.0, so grammar is unverified (contract.md:90).

Incomplete scope with no action. The version line (main.c:161) is out of scope, so scope_complete is false, and the only in scope line is a `mem avail:` report (meminfo.c:279) that carries no action. contract.md:99 makes an active earlyoom with scope_complete false a KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2 case, because the reader cannot tell whether the killer acted before the scope start. No field is asserted for earlyoom.actions here: contract.md:102 reserves actions null for an inactive or absent killer, so the counts of an active but unscoped reader are not pinned by this case.

earlyoom_journal.MESSAGE: mem avail: 12000 of 19000 MiB (63.16%), swap free: 8000 of 8192 MiB (97.66%)

cases.why: Inactive earlyoom. The show text is the real systemctl property syntax (`systemctl show earlyoom.service -p LoadState,ActiveState,UnitFileState,ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic`): LoadState=loaded with ActiveState=inactive means the unit is loaded but not running, so the state is inactive. contract.md:102 says an inactive killer reports actions null, never zero counts, so the counts are unavailable rather than zero, and the quiet verdict means no positive evidence from the killers that are readable. With no action in the journal and oomd notices at 0 the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0.

Absent earlyoom. `systemctl show` for a unit that does not exist prints LoadState=not-found with an empty UnitFileState and ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic=0, so the unit is absent rather than inactive (contract.md:90 lists both states). An absent killer reports actions null (contract.md:102), never zero counts. With nothing readable showing an action and oomd notices at 0 the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0 and the output names the unavailable killer through the null actions block.

Null journal means the journal read failed (contract.md:66). contract.md:99 makes a needed read that is null a KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2 case, and there is no positive evidence here: the show text is readable and active, the journal is null, oomd notices are 0. The action counts are unavailable, so the actions block is null. The state is still active because the show read succeeded.

Unverified version. The version line follows the main.c:161 format `earlyoom VERSION`, but the reported version is not 1.9.0, so the grammar of the messages cannot be confirmed to be the 1.9.0 grammar and grammar is unverified (contract.md:90). contract.md:99 lists an active earlyoom with an unverified grammar as a KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2 case. The version string itself is still reported verbatim, because contract.md:107 allows the version string in the output.

oomd notices. contract.md:97 makes oomd_notices greater than zero positive evidence on its own, so the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1 even though the earlyoom journal holds only the version line (main.c:161) and no action. The oomd state comes from the show text (ActiveState=active) and the notice count is the one given in the inputs.

Byte array MESSAGE. journalctl -o json renders a MESSAGE that is not valid UTF-8 as an array of byte values; contract.md:66 says such a MESSAGE is decoded as UTF-8 with replacement. The bytes here spell the kill.c:627 form `sending SIGTERM to process 4242 "imaginary-keeper"` (only the invented process name is kept, no uid and no cmdline), so after decoding the line is an in scope action and the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1 with the sigterm count at 1.

Byte array MESSAGE with an invalid UTF-8 byte. The byte 255 sits inside the invented process name of the kill.c:627 form line, so decoding as UTF-8 with replacement (contract.md:66) yields one U+FFFD inside the name. The line still starts with the action prefix `sending SIGTERM to process `, so it counts as one action and the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1. The output must not echo the message text, process name or the replacement character (contract.md:107).

Grammar line `sending SIGTERM to process ` (kill.c:627, `warn("sending %s to process %d uid %d \"%s\": ...")`). One action, so the sigterm count is 1 and the sigkill count is 0. An in scope action is positive evidence (contract.md:97), so the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1. The invented process name `imaginary-keeper` replaces the source `%s` argument; the uid and cmdline arguments are not carried into the fixture.

Grammar line `sending SIGKILL to process ` (kill.c:627 with sig_name set to SIGKILL at kill.c:621). One sigkill action and no sigterm action, so the sigkill count is 1 and the sigterm count is 0; the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1 (contract.md:97). The invented process name is `imaginary-indexer`.

Grammar line `escalating to SIGKILL after ` (kill.c:318, `warn("escalating to SIGKILL after %.3f seconds\n", secs)`), so the rendered text carries three decimals. contract.md:97 lists an escalation line as positive evidence, so the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1 with the escalation count at 1. The escalation is not an action line, so the sigterm and sigkill counts stay 0.

Grammar line `kill failed: ` (kill.c:654, `warn("kill failed: %s\n", strerror(saved_errno))`); the rendered text is the strerror text for EPERM. contract.md:97 enumerates the positive evidence as an in scope `sending SIG...to process` line, an escalation line, or oomd notices greater than zero. A failed kill line is none of those, so with no other positive evidence the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0 and only the kill_failed count is 1. This case pins the contract enumeration literally.

Grammar lines `low memory! at or below SIGTERM limits` (main.c:523) and `low memory! at or below SIGKILL limits` (main.c:519); both are warn() calls in the poll loop, and both carry PRIPCT percentages (msg.h:10), so the one digit value renders with a pad space (` 5.00%`). Two warning lines are in scope, so the low_memory_warnings count is 2. contract.md:97 does not list a low memory warning as positive evidence, so with no action line and no oomd notices the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0. This case pins the contract enumeration literally.

earlyoom_journal.MESSAGE: low memory! at or below SIGTERM limits: mem 10.00%, swap 10.00%
low memory! at or below SIGKILL limits: mem  5.00%, swap  5.00%

cases.why: Grammar line `dryrun mode enabled` (main.c:295, `warn("dryrun mode enabled, will not kill anything\n")`). The flag is set, so dryrun is true. A dry run never sends a signal, so no action line can be in scope and no positive evidence exists: the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0. The dryrun flag is not one of the positive evidence kinds in contract.md:97.

earlyoom_journal.MESSAGE: dryrun mode enabled, will not kill anything

cases.why: Version line only (main.c:161, `earlyoom VERSION`). The version parses to 1.9.0, so grammar is verified-1.9.0 and the version line is inside the scope, so scope_complete is true. No threshold line (main.c:414, main.c:416) is present, so the thresholds are unknown and the thresholds block is null, and no dryrun line (main.c:295) is present, so dryrun is false. No positive evidence, so the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0.

Adversarial near miss. The threshold lines of main.c:414 (`sending SIGTERM when mem avail <= ...`) and main.c:416 (`SIGKILL when mem avail <= ...`) start with `sending SIGTERM when`, which is not the action prefix `sending SIGTERM to process ` of kill.c:627. The lines must set the thresholds and must not be counted as actions, so the sigterm and sigkill counts stay 0 while the thresholds parse to 10.0 and 5.0 (PRIPCT, msg.h:10, pads one digit percents with a space). No positive evidence, so the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0.

earlyoom_journal.MESSAGE: sending SIGTERM when mem avail <= 10.00% and swap free <= 10.00%,
SIGKILL when mem avail <=  5.00% and swap free <=  5.00%

cases.why: Adversarial near miss. The action text `sending SIGKILL to process ` of kill.c:627 appears inside the line, but not at the start of it. contract.md:80 matches the grammar prefix anchored after stripping leading whitespace, so a mid line occurrence is not an action line. The sigkill count stays 0 and, with no other positive evidence, the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0.

Adversarial near miss. The low memory warning of main.c:519 and main.c:523 is spelled `low memory! at or below SIGTERM limits` and `low memory! at or below SIGKILL limits`, plural limits. The line here says `limit` in the singular, so it does not match either grammar prefix and the low_memory_warnings count stays 0. No positive evidence, so the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0.

earlyoom_journal.MESSAGE: low memory! at or below SIGTERM limit: mem 10.00%, swap 10.00%

cases.why: Adversarial near miss. main.c:295 warns `dryrun mode enabled, will not kill anything`; the grammar prefix is `dryrun mode enabled`. The line here says `dryrun modes enabled`, which does not start with that prefix, so the dryrun flag stays false. No positive evidence, so the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0.

earlyoom_journal.MESSAGE: dryrun modes enabled, will not kill anything

cases.why: Adversarial near miss. kill.c:654 warns `kill failed: %s`, so the grammar prefix is `kill failed: ` with the colon and the space. The line here drops the colon, so it does not match and the kill_failed count stays 0. No positive evidence, so the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0.

Null earlyoom show text means the unit read failed (contract.md:66). contract.md:99 makes a needed read that is null a KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2 case, and there is no positive evidence here: the journal is empty, the oomd state is inactive and the oomd notice count is 0. The earlyoom state is unavailable because the read failed.

Both oomd reads failed: the show text is null and the notice count is null (contract.md:66). A needed read that is null is a KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2 case (contract.md:99). The earlyoom side is readable, active and has its version line (main.c:161) in scope, but the oomd side is unknown, so the quiet verdict cannot be claimed. The oomd state is unavailable and the notice count is null.

A show text that lacks ActiveState. contract.md:99 lists it explicitly as a KILLERS_UNKNOWN exit 2 case, because the state of the unit cannot be read from the four properties. The show text here keeps LoadState, UnitFileState and ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic but omits ActiveState, so the reader must not guess the state and must not claim a quiet verdict. No field is asserted for earlyoom.state: the contract does not fix a state for a text that lacks ActiveState.

A readable and active oomd that did not notice anything. The oomd state comes from the show text (ActiveState=active) and the notice count is 0, so the oomd side holds no positive evidence (contract.md:97 needs oomd notices greater than zero). The earlyoom side is the host shaped quiet shape of c01, so the verdict is KILLERS_QUIET exit 0 with the oomd state active.

earlyoom_journal.MESSAGE: sending SIGTERM when mem avail <= 10.00% and swap free <= 10.00%,
SIGKILL when mem avail <=  5.00% and swap free <=  5.00%

cases.why: Positive evidence from the readable killer while the other killer is unreadable in action. The earlyoom unit is inactive, so its actions block is null (contract.md:102) and no earlyoom action can exist, but oomd notices greater than zero are positive evidence (contract.md:97), so the verdict is KILLER_ACTED exit 1. The quiet clause of contract.md:102 only applies when there is no positive evidence.

A needed read is null but positive evidence stands. The earlyoom journal read failed, which would make the verdict unknown (contract.md:99), but oomd notices greater than zero are positive evidence and contract.md:97 says positive evidence stands even when the scope is incomplete. The verdict is therefore KILLER_ACTED exit 1, and the oomd notice count is reported.

Setup error. The inputs schema of contract.md:66 gives earlyoom_journal as a list of entries or null; a string is neither, so the reader must fail as a setup error, exit 2 with verdict KILLERS_UNKNOWN and an error field (contract.md:105). An uncaught exception must never exit 1 (contract.md:105). The text of the error field is implementation defined and is therefore not pinned by this case; only the verdict and the exit code are.

Setup error. The inputs schema of contract.md:66 gives earlyoom_show as the text of the four systemctl properties or null; a number is neither, so the reader must fail as a setup error, exit 2 with verdict KILLERS_UNKNOWN and an error field (contract.md:105), never exit 1. The text of the error field is implementation defined and is not pinned by this case; only the verdict and the exit code are.
